canonical_claim: For a sufficiently smooth Lagrangian L and a sufficiently smooth path q with fixed endpoints, if q is stationary for the action integral A(q) = integral L(t, q(t), q'(t)) dt with respect to every admissible endpoint-fixing variation, then q satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation on the interior of the time interval.

scope_boundary.data: a finite-dimensional real configuration space (initially Euclidean), a compact real time interval [a,b], a C2 Lagrangian, and a C2 path q
scope_boundary.hypotheses: all endpoint-fixing C1 test variations have zero first variation; differentiability and integrability hypotheses justify differentiation under the integral and integration by parts
scope_boundary.conclusion: the time derivative of the velocity derivative of L equals the position derivative of L along q on the open interval
scope_boundary.excluded: The converse, constrained systems, nonsmooth paths, fields, infinite-dimensional configuration spaces, and the claim that every physical trajectory globally minimizes action

degenerate_cases: A zero-length time interval is excluded from the interior differential conclusion.
Constant paths remain admissible when they meet the fixed endpoints.
Stationarity must not be strengthened to a global or local minimum without additional convexity or second-variation hypotheses.
